# Jack Schliewe

> AI developer and security engineer in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Builds ref-radar, prior art for coding agents.

## ref-radar

ref-radar answers "who already built this, where do I start reading, and can I reuse it?" for coding agents. Every ref has a why line, start-here paths pinned to a commit, and a reuse verdict from its license (copy, copyleft or study).

- MCP server (streamable HTTP, no account needed to read): https://ref.lookit.space/mcp
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http ref-radar https://ref.lookit.space/mcp`
- Instructions for agents: https://ref.lookit.space/llms.txt
- Catalog: https://ref.lookit.space/catalog.json
- Nightly export: https://github.com/thecandylane/ref-radar-data

## Posts

- [An agent pentests Juice Shop: 25 findings for $0.68, checked](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/an-agent-pentests-juice-shop) (2026-11-18). One saved run of an open-source pentest agent against a deliberately vulnerable app: what it found, how much of it holds up against its own evidence, what it missed, and what kept it on target.
- [Reading RISC-V by hand: finishing a disassembler from 2023](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/reading-risc-v-by-hand) (2026-11-18). How one 32-bit word turns back into an instruction, the three bugs a hand-written decoder runs into, and a disassembler you can run on this page.
- [ref-radar, prior art for a coding agent](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/ref-radar) (2026-11-18). What ref.lookit.space answers, how an agent reads it, and what the catalog and the site counted in the week ending 18 November 2026.
- [Three red-team tools against my own agent](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/three-red-team-tools-one-agent) (2026-11-18). I pointed promptfoo, garak and PyRIT at a local copy of this site's agent CTF. Here is what each one found, what a gate in code changed, and what a small local model can and can't tell you.
- [Cyber Trials 2026: five rooms and the bugs behind them](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/cyber-trials-2026) (2026-11-17). What my team and I ran into at TryHackMe's Cyber Trials: the bug behind each room, why it was there, and how a defender would catch or fix it.
- [Defanging Shai-Hulud: keeping a worm you never run](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/defanging-shai-hulud) (2026-11-17). How I kept a copy of the Shai-Hulud npm worm for study, safe to open in an editor or hand to a coding agent, without running a single byte of it.
- [How this site sees you, and so does every other one](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/how-this-site-sees-you) (2026-11-17). A tour of /you: what your connection, your browser, your typing, your photos and your passwords give away to any site, how each one is measured, and what blunts it.
- [Shai-Hulud: ten waves, one shape](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/shai-hulud-ten-waves) (2026-11-17). Every public report on the Shai-Hulud npm worm, from September 2025 to October 2026, read side by side. The payload changed every time. The shape never did, and that shape is what you can check for.
- [Three bugs, one model](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/three-bugs-one-model) (2026-11-17). Chrome needed two separate bugs for one code execution this year. Here is the chain, and what a small engine can honestly reproduce of it.
- [What 194 flagged repos look like](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/what-194-flagged-repos-look-like) (2026-11-17). ref-radar marks some repos "dangerous code: read, don't run". I had an agent read every one of them: what's really in there, the shapes that repeat, the repos built to fool AI agents, and where my own scanner gets it wrong.
- [Writing an engine to break it](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/writing-an-engine-to-break-it) (2026-11-17). A checker that reads your exploit source is a quiz. To make a bug real, I had to write the machine it lives in.
- [How this site is built](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/how-this-site-is-built) (2026-11-16). Posts are MDX files in git. The intro paragraph wraps around a radar you can drag. Every repo a post mentions is a live card from ref-radar.
- [The familiar: an agent CTF on this site](https://schliewesystems.com/blog/the-familiar-agent-ctf) (2026-11-16). This site has an AI agent with tools, and a flag hidden on its host. The agent will refuse to give it to you. Your job is to make it anyway.
